source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section II: Benefits and uses of corn
text:
Corn is an important crop that provides many benefits to both humans and animals. Within corn crops, damage/loss during storage varies by variety, roughly: ice/cold-storage type losses 10.8%, other-variety type losses 10%, snack-type losses 4.3%, feed/livestock-type losses 73.4%, and rat/pest losses 1.4%, among others (note: these percentages, as transcribed from the source table, are difficult to read with full confidence and are reported here as printed; a plausible alternative reading is that these are nutrient-composition percentages of the corn kernel — water, protein, oil, carbohydrate, and fiber/ash — rather than loss percentages; this discrepancy in interpretation should be flagged rather than guessed).

1. Corn as human food: Corn must be prepared as a staple food for some countries. Corn is also eaten as a supplementary food alongside people's usual staple food.

2. Corn as raw material for industry: Corn is used as raw material for the animal feed and livestock industry.

3. Corn for scientific research: Corn has properties that make it useful to scientists for studying genetics and hybridization/cross-breeding characteristics of one or several grass-family species, since corn belongs to the grass family.
